amends: SSCTR-V1FC-DECISION-r1 and Amendment 1 (neither edited). Items not named here stand as decided.
reviewer: The same SSCTR-1.0.0 instance that authored r1 and Amendment 1, as decision author. An AI agent with no human credentials; no human, clinical or empirical validation. The independent SSCTR judge keeps judging the implementation; this instance does not judge it.
authority: PROVISIONAL_INTERNAL_DOMAIN_AUTHORITY, nonclinical sporting content only; clinical judgment stays CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED.
trigger: Judge finding R-01 (MAJOR, marathon only), as relayed by the Chief: race day reads the program's highest executed long run however old, so a 150-minute run executed about 77 days before the race keeps race day at marathon effort after ten weeks of missed long runs. This contradicts the 30-day recency of B1.2 and r1 G.2. The reproduction and probes were not re-run by this instance.
literature: No new search. The 30-day window reuses SRC06 (Frandsen 2025, full text: risk is defined against the longest run of the previous 30 days) and the r1 completion rationale (SRC11).

value.window: sessions on days 21 to 50 before the race inclusive (1 to 30 days before the first taper day, which is 20 days before the race)
value.candidates: executed training long runs (role LONG) by their executed minutes; never taper or race-window sessions, the race, post-event sessions or easy, quality, restart or walk/jog sessions

conditions: Marathon only. 10K and half marathon keep the existing achievedPeakBasis and stay byte-identical (r1 G.1).
The windowed value below 150 makes race day a completion, and Amendment 1's caution applies: EVENT_AMBITIOUS_FOR_CURRENT_RUNNING with the later or shorter event first, keeping the race offered.
Mode and history completions (WALK_JOG, RESTART, RETURN) are unchanged and apply in addition.

Read from the record by executed date. A reprojection before race week uses the same window, with projected weeks counted as executed, as the existing conditional projection does, so a shortfall appears as soon as it is projected (Amendment 1, B3.planCreationDisclosure).
items.rationale: Race-day readiness for a 5-6 hour event must rest on recent long-run capacity, as the single-run ceiling and B1.2 already do. A 30-day window before the taper holds four (sometimes five) long-run days, so it tolerates a consolidation week and one or two missed long runs (as the judge's probes show), yet catches a long absence. A longer window would recreate R-01; a shorter one would make a single missed run decisive.

conditions: Training long runs executed in the plan but outside the window count for nothing in the race-day mode, the keep caution or the taper long run.
They stay in the record and in every other existing rule unchanged (single-run ceiling within its own 30 days, gates, next-block resume, which the ceiling still caps).
items.rationale: Old capacity is not current capacity; giving it partial weight would need a decay rule no evidence supports.

value.noCandidate: the taper long run is that week's easy run (existing longRunFloor)

conditions: Marathon only, and only the taper long run. Taper easy-run and quality fractions keep their existing achieved-peak basis, still bound by the single-run ceiling and the gates.
Taper long runs stay capped by the single-run ceiling (unchanged).
items.rationale: One basis for the race-day decision and the taper long run keeps the plan coherent: a taper is a reduction from what the athlete has recently done (SRC01, SRC02), not from an old peak.

value.atPlanCreation: Add to the Amendment 1 creation disclosure: 'Race day is decided by the longest long run you complete between about 7 and 3 weeks before the race.'
value.atCompletion: When the windowed value decides a completion, the EVENT_AMBITIOUS_FOR_CURRENT_RUNNING statement names the longest long run executed in that window (0 when none) as the reason, and says that earlier long runs are too long ago to count.

conditions: Wording with Product/UX; content fixed as above.
items.rationale: The athlete must know which runs decide race day, and why an earlier long run no longer counts.

proposedQueueItems.change: the race-day and taper long-run basis is the 30-day pre-taper window

proposedQueueNote: Proposals only; nothing appended; the queue stays at 235.
hostInjectedContext: As in r1: a global CLAUDE.md, the project CLAUDE.md and a MEMORY.md were injected and used only to orient.
verificationNeeded: The R-01 reproduction yields a completion with the caution; the fully executed reference athlete and the athlete missing only the last two specific long runs keep marathon effort; the taper long run follows the windowed basis; 10K and half byte-identical.
expiry: As r1; also on any change to the taper length, race window or long-run cadence, since the window is defined from them.
